fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Fenced Sections
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Install a reflective marker or sign identifying the rear access point so responders can locate it quickly under low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the rear access route clear of parked vehicles so responders can reach the back of the property without delay.
• If rear-access gates are present in fenced sections, keep them unlocked or secured with a single cut-able lock to allow rapid entry.
• Mark any gate latches or releases that are not immediately visible so responders can open them quickly without searching.
• Keep the parking area clear of stored items so it can serve as a staging area for emergency equipment if needed.
• Confirm that the access drive can support the weight and turning radius of a fire apparatus or ambulance.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; None Visible
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin scattered trees near structures so their branches do not touch or hang over rooflines.
• Cut or mow grass growing directly against the foundation and along the base of any outbuildings.
• Remove dead grass and dry plant material from open areas immediately surrounding the house.
• Keep low-hanging branches on scattered trees trimmed up from the ground to reduce the path fire can travel from grass into the tree canopy.
• Maintain clear, open ground between shrub clusters and the house so there is no continuous path of plant material leading to the structure.
